toolCalls.name: StructuredOutput

output.brief:
The slowdown comes from the May credit policy refresh, not from Corvane or the new hires. Since 2 May, property-secured loans between $150k and $500k must have a full appraisal instead of a desktop valuation. The valuation firm takes about 8.6 days for a full appraisal and about 1.2 for a desktop one, and those times haven't changed. Valuation-stage time on property-secured loans rose from about 1.7 days to about 8 days. Unsecured loans are back to about 5.9 days, and consumer loans on Corvane are flat. Document collection at the five branches with new hires matches the other branches. The Hub's underwriting and decision stages are flat. So withholding Corvane's payment or putting new hires on improvement plans would punish the wrong parties and fix nothing.

Withdrawals are partly an artifact. Corvane auto-closes files after 30 days without an upload and counts them as withdrawn. That accounts for 32 of 73 closures. Only 14 customers said they financed elsewhere. I can't show that slow approvals are driving abandonment.

Next step: take the measured delay and the policy's risk rationale to the credit risk committee, and ask whether to amend the mandatory full-appraisal rule for the $150k–$500k band. Also add a by-stage breakdown to the dashboard. I'm fairly confident (about 85%).
